title: KAFKA-16517; Do not decode metadata records in the internal kraft partition listener
body:
The internal kraft partition listener KRaftControlRecordStateMachine
only tracks control records. When it reads the log and the snapshot it
also decodes every data record through RecordsIterator, allocating a
buffer and running the serde for each record even though the decoded
data records are never used.

This change lets the caller of a records or snapshot reader pick which
records it wants decoded, so the ones it does not need are never
decoded.

This PR uses a new RecordsDecodingStrategy to tell RecordsIterator, per
batch, whether to decode the control/data records; unwanted records
become a Batch.skipped that carries only the offset information without
reading the bytes. It is created via dataAndControl, controlOnly,
dataOnly, none. The internal kraft partition listener now uses
controlOnly on both its log and snapshot read paths.

Reviewers: Kevin Wu <kwu@confluent.io>, José Armando García Sancio
 <jsancio@apache.org>

files.patch:
@@ -221,4 +221,42 @@ public static <T> Batch<T> data(
             List.of()
         );
     }
+
+    /**
+     * Create a batch whose records were skipped, carrying only the offset information without the
+     * record bytes.
+     *
+     * @param baseOffset offset of the first record in the batch
+     * @param epoch epoch of the leader that created this batch
+     * @param appendTimestamp timestamp in milliseconds of when the batch was appended
+     * @param sizeInBytes number of bytes used by this batch
+     * @param numRecords the number of records in this batch
+     */
+    public static <T> Batch<T> skipped(
+        long baseOffset,
+        int epoch,
+        long appendTimestamp,
+        int sizeInBytes,
+        int numRecords
+    ) {
+        if (numRecords < 1) {
+            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
+                String.format(
+                    "Batch must contain at least one record; baseOffset = %d; epoch = %d",
+                    baseOffset,
+                    epoch
+                )
+            );
+        }
+
+        return new Batch<>(
+            baseOffset,
+            epoch,
+            appendTimestamp,
+            sizeInBytes,
+            baseOffset + numRecords - 1,
+            List.of(),
+            List.of()
+        );
+    }
 }
